title: GPU account topology, CI burst playbook and cost smoothing
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary

This playbook documents the recommended account/VPC topology, CI-driven burst workflow, Terraform/IaC patterns, and runbook steps used when we safely burst GPU capacity for large evals or time-limited customer spikes. It focuses on multi-account isolation, predictable egress, deterministic cost allocation, and fast fallback if capacity or networking fails.

Scope

- Applies to ephemeral and reserved GPU bursting initiated from the CI/CD pipeline (eval clusters, batch training windows, large-scale inference tests).
- Covers AWS and GCP patterns currently in use by fleet-manager and burst-orchestrator services.
- Excludes long-lived Dedicated customer pools and on-prem private deployments (see eng-private-deployments for those patterns).

Goals and constraints

- Predictable unit economics per-burst (target variance < 12% per month).
- Minimal production impact: experimental bursts must not affect hosted API SLOs (99th pct latency) or reduce reserved Dedicated capacity below guaranteed thresholds.
- Clear ownership and automated rollback for failed bursts.

Account and VPC topology (recommended)

High-level pattern: Central orchestration account -> Tenant/burst accounts -> Egress account

1) orchestration-account (owned by infra-core)
   - Services: fleet-manager, burst-orchestrator, billing-sidecar
   - Purpose: coordinates allocations, holds IAM roles assumed by burst accounts
2) burst-<env>-account(s) (owned by infra-team or feature team)
   - Short-lived accounts created by CI (names: burst-ci-<job-id>)
   - Houses ephemeral GPU pools and ephemeral VPCs
3) egress-account (owned by networking)
   - Central NAT/egress proxies, shared forward proxies, egress metering and billing export
VPC design notes:

- Burst VPCs should be created with a single private subnet per AZ and one small public subnet for admin bastion (if needed).
- Use VPC endpoints for S3/GCS, ECR/Artifact Registry. Avoid internet egress except through egress-account proxies.
- Enforce egress TLS intercept via egress-account appliances to ensure metering and policy.

Tagging and cost allocation matrix

| Tag key | Required on | Purpose |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| redwood:burst-id | EC2/GCE instance, cluster, node-pool | Unique identifier for the CI job (burst-ci-12345) |
| redwood:team | All resources | Chargeback mapping |
| redwood:project | Cluster, workspace | Product or experiment name |
| redwood:owner | IAM role or user | Rotation and oncall contact |
Enforcement: Apply via Terraform module input variables and CI job metadata. Billing exports must map these tags to internal ledger.

CI/CD driven burst workflow (end-to-end)

High-level flow:

1) CI job requests capacity via the burst RPC (orchestration-account) with payload: desired gpus, region, max_cost_usd, expected_duration_minutes, tags.
2) burst-orchestrator validates policy (quota, tenant SLOs, egress constraints) and creates a temporary account or assumes a provisioning role in a pre-provisioned burst account.
3) Terraform in CI runs a scoped module (see Terraform modules below) to create node pools and attach to test eval cluster.
4) CI waits until health checks pass (kube nodes Ready && nvtop reporting devices visible).
5) Workload runs; monitoring exports token-level or GPU-minute counters to billing pipeline.

Success criteria: CI marks job success if workload completes and billing delta <= max_cost_usd. Failure criteria trigger rollback.

Terraform modules and IaC patterns

Principles:
- Modules must be idempotent, accept explicit cost/tags, and be small (single responsibility).
- Keep account bootstrapping separate from burst provisioning modules.
- All state lives in a per-burst remote state with short TTL (S3 or GCS bucket with lifecycle 30d).

Key modules (recommended):
- module/gpu-burst-nodepool: creates GPU node pool, autoscaling policy, gpu-driver DaemonSet reference
- module/burst-vpc: minimal VPC, endpoints, route to egress-account
- module/iam-provision-role: role with least privilege for burst CI to apply IaC
- module/egress-attachment: attaches egress proxies and configures routing

Example Terraform snippet (simplified) - include in appendix for copy/paste.

Operational runbook: emergency burst fallback

Use this when a burst job is impacting production or exceeding cost limits.

1) Alert triggers: cost spike > 1.5x estimate OR API error rate increase impacting hosted-api (SLO breach).
2) Triage owner (oncall infra) pings #infra-burst and runs anchored diagnostics.
   - CLI: burstctl status --burst-id <id>
   - kubectl: kubectl --context burst-<id> get nodes
   - cloud: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:redwood:burst-id,Values=<id>
3) If networking is the cause, run egress-proxy-healthcheck:
   - curl -f https://egress-proxy.internal/health || escalate to networking
4) Emergency rollback (automated preferred):
   - burstctl cancel --burst-id <id> --reason "auto-rollback-cost-guard"  
   - This triggers Terraform destroy in the burst account and detaches volumes.
5) Post-incident: run cost reconciliation and mark job in ledger. If rollback failed, open a PagerDuty for infra-core.

Monitoring, alerts, and metrics

Core metrics to emit for every burst:
- gpu.node.count (gauge)
- gpu.utilization.p95 (percentage)
- burst.cost.estimate_usd and burst.cost.actual_usd
- network.egress.bytes_per_minute (per-burst)
- burst.healthy (boolean)

Alert thresholds (examples):
- Cost overrun: actual_usd > estimate_usd * 1.25 -> critical alert to infra-cost
- Network egress sudden jump: delta > 10x baseline over 5m -> page networking
- Node readiness lag: nodes not Ready after 10 minutes -> warn to #infra-burst

Rollout and ownership

- Owners: infra-core (fleet provisioning), networking (egress-account), infra-cost (billing reconciliation).
- For any new burst-capable CI job, request a design review with infra-core and infra-cost. Use template: BURST-REQUEST-YYYYMMDD.
- Quarterly audits: verify tagging fidelity and cost variance targets.

Appendix: CLI and Terraform examples

Minimal Terraform example (pseudocode)

module "burst_vpc" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.internal/terraform-modules//burst-vpc"
  name   = "burst-ci-${var.job_id}"
  tags = {
    "redwood:burst-id" = var.job_id
    "redwood:team" = var.team
  }
}

module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.internal/terraform-modules//gpu-burst-nodepool"
  region = var.region
  gpu_count = var.gpu_count
  max_price_usd = var.max_cost_usd
  tags = module.burst_vpc.tags
}

CI snippet (shell)

export JOB_ID="burst-ci-${BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER}"
export REGION="us-west-2"
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=burst-state-${JOB_ID}" \  && terraform apply -var "job_id=${JOB_ID}" -auto-approve

Verification checklist (CI)

- [ ] cloud instances tagged with redwood:burst-id
- [ ] nodes Ready in kube (kubectl get nodes)
- [ ] nvml visible on nodes (ssh + nvidia-smi)
- [ ] billing export lines include burst-id
